title: Trace-normalized finite exceptional core comparisons
statement: For a finite-field datum D, prime l distinct from D.p, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l in an independent universe, separated finite-type D.k-schemes X,Y, a separated finite-type D.k-morphism f:X to Y, its compactification c, common-stage dualities BX,BY [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], and an exceptional coefficient system S, there exists a FiniteExceptionalFormulaCore t [lem-coef-qbar-finite-exceptional-formula-core] for which every finite identification adjunction is trace-normalized in the sense of DualFormulaAdjunctionNormalized [lem-sf-rational-dual-formula-adjunction]. This conclusion imposes no scalar square.

source.place: Retained thm-coef-qbar-verdier proof step 9: trace-normalized finite comparisons and substitution of finite-origin scalar squares

proof.text: Take any finite core. At every finite coefficient field choose the trace-normalized dual-formula adjunction. Right-adjoint uniqueness compares it with the system adjunction transported along rationalLeft. Transporting by this comparison recovers the chosen adjunction, as follows by counit extensionality.

Replace each old finite identification by this comparison. Conjugate the old common-stage comparison by the inclusion of the new comparison followed by the inverse old comparison. Whiskering and composition give a natural isomorphism. Cancellation of the old comparison with its inverse gives normalized, and the adjunction equality gives its trace normalization.

theorem finite_exceptional_normalized_core
    (BX : Duality D l hl Ω X) (BY : Duality D l hl Ω Y)
    (c : Compactification f)
    (S : ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.System l (AuxiliaryClosure.{u} l) D hl (f := f)) :
    ∃ t : FiniteExceptionalFormulaCore D l hl Ω X f BX BY c S,
      ∀ E : Index l Ω,
        RationalOperations.DualFormulaAdjunctionNormalized D l hl X c (fieldStage l Ω E)
          (BX.finite.omega E) (BY.finite.omega E) (BX.finite.datum E) (BY.finite.datum E)
          (t.finite E).adjunction
